name: google-flights/calendar
description: Get the lowest Google Flights fare for each departure date in a range between two airports, for one-way or round trips.

gl.description: Parameter defines the country to use for the Google Flights search. It's a two-letter country code. (e.g., `us` for the United States, `uk` for United Kingdom, or `fr` for France) Head to the Google countries page for a full list of supported Google countries.

hl.description: Parameter defines the language to use for the Google Flights search. It's a two-letter language code. (e.g., `en` for English, `es` for Spanish, or `fr` for French). Head to the Google languages page for a full list of supported Google languages.

type.description: Parameter defines the type of the flights. Available options: `1` - Round trip (default) `2` - One way

stops.description: Parameter defines the number of stops during the flight. Available options: `0` - Any number of stops (default) `1` - Nonstop only `2` - 1 stop or fewer `3` - 2 stops or fewer

adults.description: Parameter defines the number of adults. Default to 1.

children.description: Parameter defines the number of children. Default to 0.

currency.description: Parameter defines the currency of the returned prices. Default to `USD`. Head to the Google Travel Currencies page for a full list of supported currency codes.

arrival_id.description: Parameter defines the arrival airport code or location kgmid. An airport code is an uppercase 3-letter code. You can search for it on Google Flights or IATA. For example, `CDG` is Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport and `AUS` is Austin-Bergstrom International Airport. A location kgmid is a string that starts with `/m/`. You can search for a location on Wikidata and use its "Freebase ID" as the location kgmid. For example, `/m/0vzm` is the location kgmid for Austin, TX.

departure_id.description: Parameter defines the departure airport code or location kgmid. An airport code is an uppercase 3-letter code. You can search for it on Google Flights or IATA. For example, `CDG` is Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport and `AUS` is Austin-Bergstrom International Airport. A location kgmid is a string that starts with `/m/`. You can search for a location on Wikidata and use its "Freebase ID" as the location kgmid. For example, `/m/0vzm` is the location kgmid for Austin, TX.

return_times.description: Parameter defines the return times range. It's a string containing two (for departure only) or four (for departure and arrival) comma-separated numbers. Each number represents the beginning of an hour. For example: `4,18`: 4:00 AM - 7:00 PM departure `0,18`: 12:00 AM - 7:00 PM departure `19,23`: 7:00 PM - 12:00 AM departure `4,18,3,19`: 4:00 AM - 7:00 PM departure, 3:00 AM - 8:00 PM arrival `0,23,3,19`: unrestricted departure, 3:00 AM - 8:00 PM arrival Parameter should only be used when `type` parameter is set to: `1` (Round trip)

travel_class.description: Parameter defines the travel class. Available options: `1` - Economy (default) `2` - Premium economy `3` - Business `4` - First

date_range_end.description: Parameter defines the end date of the date range. The format is YYYY-MM-DD. e.g. `2026-12-31` Default to end of next month.

infants_on_lap.description: Parameter defines the number of infants on lap. Default to 0.

outbound_times.description: Parameter defines the outbound times range. It's a string containing two (for departure only) or four (for departure and arrival) comma-separated numbers. Each number represents the beginning of an hour. For example: `4,18`: 4:00 AM - 7:00 PM departure `0,18`: 12:00 AM - 7:00 PM departure `19,23`: 7:00 PM - 12:00 AM departure `4,18,3,19`: 4:00 AM - 7:00 PM departure, 3:00 AM - 8:00 PM arrival `0,23,3,19`: unrestricted departure, 3:00 AM - 8:00 PM arrival

infants_in_seat.description: Parameter defines the number of infants in seat. Default to 0.

json_restrictor.description: Parameter defines the fields you want to include in the output, reducing payload size for faster response. See the JSON Restrictor documentation for more details.

round_trip_days.description: Parameter defines the number of days for the round trip. Default to 7. It can only be used in combination with `type` parameter set to `1` (Round trip). Parameter cannot be used with `fixed_outbound_date` parameter.

date_range_start.description: Parameter defines the start date of the date range. The format is YYYY-MM-DD. e.g. `2026-11-12` Default to today's date. When `fixed_outbound_date` is set to `true`, this date is also used as the outbound date.

exclude_airlines.description: Parameter defines the airline codes to be excluded. Split multiple airlines with comma. It can't be used together with `include_airlines`. Each airline code should be a 2-character IATA code consisting of either two uppercase letters or one uppercase letter and one digit. You can search for airline codes on IATA. For example, `UA` is United Airlines. Additionally, alliances can be also included here: `STAR_ALLIANCE` - Star Alliance `SKYTEAM` - SkyTeam `ONEWORLD` - Oneworld `exclude_airlines` and `include_airlines` parameters can't be used together.

include_airlines.description: Parameter defines the airline codes to be included. Split multiple airlines with comma. It can't be used together with `exclude_airlines`. Each airline code should be a 2-character IATA code consisting of either two uppercase letters or one uppercase letter and one digit. You can search for airline codes on IATA. For example, `UA` is United Airlines. Additionally, alliances can be also included here: `STAR_ALLIANCE` - Star Alliance `SKYTEAM` - SkyTeam `ONEWORLD` - Oneworld `exclude_airlines` and `include_airlines` parameters can't be used together.

fixed_outbound_date.description: Parameter defines whether the outbound date is fixed. It can be set to `true` to depart on `date_range_start` and get a price for each return date in the date range, or `false` (default) to get a price for each outbound date in the date range with a trip length of `round_trip_days`. It can only be used in combination with `type` parameter set to `1` (Round trip). Parameter cannot be used with `round_trip_days` parameter.

# Google Flights Calendar

Get the lowest Google Flights fare for each departure date in a range between two airports, for one-way or round trips.

## Request

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.sandbase.ai/v1/api/google-flights/calendar" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SANDBASE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"departure_id": "AUS", "arrival_id": "JFK"}'
```

The result is returned in `outputs[0].data` as structured JSON.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `departure_id` | string | Yes | Parameter defines the departure airport code or location kgmid. An airport code is an uppercase 3-letter code. You can search for it on Google Flights or IATA. For example, `CDG` is Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport and `AUS` is Austin-Bergst |
| `arrival_id` | string | Yes | Parameter defines the arrival airport code or location kgmid. An airport code is an uppercase 3-letter code. You can search for it on Google Flights or IATA. For example, `CDG` is Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport and `AUS` is Austin-Bergstro |
| `gl` | string | No | Parameter defines the country to use for the Google Flights search. It's a two-letter country code. (e.g., `us` for the United States, `uk` for United Kingdom, or `fr` for France) Head to the Google countries page for a full list of support |
| `hl` | string | No | Parameter defines the language to use for the Google Flights search. It's a two-letter language code. (e.g., `en` for English, `es` for Spanish, or `fr` for French). Head to the Google languages page for a full list of supported Google lang |
| `currency` | string | No | Parameter defines the currency of the returned prices. Default to `USD`. Head to the Google Travel Currencies page for a full list of supported currency codes. |
| `type` | string | No | Parameter defines the type of the flights. Available options: `1` - Round trip (default) `2` - One way |
| `date_range_start` | string | No | Parameter defines the start date of the date range. The format is YYYY-MM-DD. e.g. `2026-11-12` Default to today's date. When `fixed_outbound_date` is set to `true`, this date is also used as the outbound date. |
| `date_range_end` | string | No | Parameter defines the end date of the date range. The format is YYYY-MM-DD. e.g. `2026-12-31` Default to end of next month. |
| `round_trip_days` | string | No | Parameter defines the number of days for the round trip. Default to 7. It can only be used in combination with `type` parameter set to `1` (Round trip). Parameter cannot be used with `fixed_outbound_date` parameter. |
| `fixed_outbound_date` | string | No | Parameter defines whether the outbound date is fixed. It can be set to `true` to depart on `date_range_start` and get a price for each return date in the date range, or `false` (default) to get a price for each outbound date in the date ran |
| `travel_class` | string | No | Parameter defines the travel class. Available options: `1` - Economy (default) `2` - Premium economy `3` - Business `4` - First |
| `adults` | string | No | Parameter defines the number of adults. Default to 1. |
| `children` | string | No | Parameter defines the number of children. Default to 0. |
| `infants_in_seat` | string | No | Parameter defines the number of infants in seat. Default to 0. |
| `infants_on_lap` | string | No | Parameter defines the number of infants on lap. Default to 0. |
| `stops` | string | No | Parameter defines the number of stops during the flight. Available options: `0` - Any number of stops (default) `1` - Nonstop only `2` - 1 stop or fewer `3` - 2 stops or fewer |
| `exclude_airlines` | string | No | Parameter defines the airline codes to be excluded. Split multiple airlines with comma. It can't be used together with `include_airlines`. Each airline code should be a 2-character IATA code consisting of either two uppercase letters or one |
| `include_airlines` | string | No | Parameter defines the airline codes to be included. Split multiple airlines with comma. It can't be used together with `exclude_airlines`. Each airline code should be a 2-character IATA code consisting of either two uppercase letters or one |
| `outbound_times` | string | No | Parameter defines the outbound times range. It's a string containing two (for departure only) or four (for departure and arrival) comma-separated numbers. Each number represents the beginning of an hour. For example: `4,18`: 4:00 AM - 7:00  |
| `return_times` | string | No | Parameter defines the return times range. It's a string containing two (for departure only) or four (for departure and arrival) comma-separated numbers. Each number represents the beginning of an hour. For example: `4,18`: 4:00 AM - 7:00 PM |
| `json_restrictor` | string | No | Parameter defines the fields you want to include in the output, reducing payload size for faster response. See the JSON Restrictor documentation for more details. |

## Pricing

$0.010 per successful call. Failed calls are not charged.
